Definition: to plan, usually in a bad sense
BiblicalUsage: zâmam means to plan, usually in a bad sense. In Genesis 11:6 we read, "And the LORD said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do..." It appears again in Deuteronomy 19:19: "Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother..."
TheologicalSignificance: zamam is to plan, usually in a bad sense, and I believe it shows me something true about the way God made the world.
